more.title: Tiny photosynthetic organisms help transport carbon to the depths of the Baltic Sea
more.summary: Tiny photosynthetic organisms in the Baltic Sea can contribute substantially to the transport of carbon from surface waters to deeper parts of the sea. A new study from the Department of Ecology, Environment and Plant Sciences at Stockholm University shows that their ability to form colonies and aggregates is an important factor determining how much of their biomass sinks.

more.title: Cost of Canadian wildfires could top $2 trillion over the 21st century, study shows
more.summary: Failure to curb global warming now could cost future generations of Canadians trillions of dollars in wildfire impacts alone, according to a new Simon Fraser University study. The study is among the first to put a price tag on projected Canadian wildfire activity driven by climate change.

more.title: NASA’s Webb finds signs of Mars-sized worlds smashing together
more.summary: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope is giving astronomers a glimpse of the kinds of violent collisions that may have shaped our own solar system, including the giant impact thought to have created the Moon. By studying 21 rare “extreme debris disks” around young stars, researchers found that their dust can reveal the scale and intensity of planetary collisions.

more.title: Superbug P. aeruginosa uses two protein plugs to seal channels against antibiotics
more.summary: A joint research team has identified a new mechanism underlying antibiotic resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a major multidrug-resistant "superbug." The discovery provides important clues for the development of new treatments for multidrug-resistant bacterial infections. The findings are published in the journal Nature Communications.

more.title: International experience gives business leaders an edge, study finds
more.summary: Business leaders with international experience play a significant role in shaping the success of their organizations and are often associated with stronger organizational performance, including higher growth, profitability and stock market performance, according to a new study published in the Journal of Management.

more.title: Webb finds a surprising atmosphere on a scorching lava world
more.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has found strong evidence that the rocky lava world HD 3167 b has an atmosphere, despite circling its star every 24 hours under extreme heat. The surprising discovery could help scientists understand how rocky planets retain atmospheres and what the young, molten Earth may once have looked like.

more.title: Nobel physics winner's pride at pioneering AI role
more.summary: Francis Halzen, winner of the Nobel Prize in physics, spoke with pride on Wednesday about his early promotion of artificial intelligence in his research on neutrinos.

more.title: Chain reaction that begins when tumor suppression gene is switched off offers clues to how cancer develops
more.summary: A tumor suppressor gene known as p53 is mutated in more than half of all cancers, but how it acts to prevent cancer formation is largely unknown. A study by UT Southwestern Medical Center researchers sheds light on this phenomenon by showing what happens when p53 becomes disabled, revealing the gene's diverse roles in maintaining healthy metabolic activity, repressing mobile genes called retrotransposons and…

more.title: Offshore wind turbine foundations may cool ocean surface by mixing seawater
more.summary: New research within the PELAgIO ECOWind project has revealed how offshore wind farms can influence ocean temperatures and mixing, and why their effects depend on local conditions.

more.title: Healthleap raises $38M for its AI that flags hospital patients who may need a closer look
more.author: Ram Iyer
more.summary: The financing includes an $8M seed round co-led by Sequoia Capital and First Round Capital, and a $30 million Series A led by Hummingbird Ventures.

more.title: Bloom raises $3.6M to become the ‘Alibaba’ of American manufacturing
more.author: Sean O'Kane
more.summary: The Detroit startup has widened its scope beyond mobility to help drone and robotics companies find U.S.-based manufacturers, shippers, and more.

more.title: Long Island measurements reveal household products and buildings as major summer pollution sources
more.summary: Products such as hairspray, paint and household disinfectants are increasingly causing summertime air pollution—and cities aren't accounting for it, which makes it harder to issue air quality advisories and enact regulations, new research from Colorado State University, the University of Minnesota and Purdue University shows.

more.title: Eight-year analysis reveals how sunlight and nutrients shape sustainable urban farming
more.summary: Factors such as sunlight and stage-specific nutrient application determine crop success in urban agriculture, far beyond fixed recipes or miracle solutions. The findings are published in the journal Agronomy for Sustainable Development.

more.title: Hawaiian hot spot study uncovers evidence of true polar wander
more.summary: On Earth, everything is moving. The planet spins, the tectonic plates shift and the spin axis wobbles, as do the magnetic poles, which makes determining how things move a rather tricky proposition. For Rice University's Richard Gordon, this problem came up when he was trying to understand the history of the Hawaiian hot spot, the deep-mantle source of the volcanism that created the Hawaiian–Emperor chain of islands…

more.title: New approach to plant stress studies could yield hardier crops and medical insights
more.summary: At the University of Missouri, plant scientist Ron Mittler is rewriting the playbook for how scientists study life by asking what happens when living organisms face multiple stresses at once.

more.title: Undergraduate student may have solved puzzle regarding isolated galaxies that have stopped producing stars
more.summary: An undergraduate astrophysics student at UC Berkeley has found three unusual galaxies—cataloged as Shapiro Dwarf Galaxies I, II and III. Each galaxy is far from other galaxies and has stopped making stars, a combination that is extremely rare. The discovery, published in The Astrophysical Journal, provides compelling observational evidence of a long-held astronomical theory.

more.title: Another personal AI assistant has launched — Meet Tab, which emerged from stealth with a $300M valuation
more.author: Dominic-Madori Davis
more.summary: A new personal AI assistant has arrived. Meet Tab, which announced Tuesday that it had officially emerged from stealth.

more.title: As AI Closed In on ‘Unique Games’ Proof, Researchers Raced to Beat the Machines
more.author: Ben Brubaker
more.summary: In the shadow of a rumored AI proof of one of the biggest problems in their field, three computer scientists rushed to publish their own milestone result. The post As AI Closed In on ‘Unique Games’ Proof, Researchers Raced to Beat the Machines first appeared on Quanta Magazine

more.title: New collar sensor could reveal how wildfire smoke affects animal health
more.summary: When wildfire smoke fills the air, most people can go inside to avoid it. Wildlife does not have that option, and little is known about how animals living in remote areas respond to wildfires and smoke exposure.

more.title: California amps up pressure on grid buildouts that take too long
more.author: Jeff St. John
more.summary: This is California Wire , a weekly newsletter from Jeff St. John on the state’s clean energy transition. Subscribe to get it every Wednesday via Substack. Welcome back to California Wire! This week, I want to dive into a topic that’s both timely and timeless: transmission lines, and how long it takes to build…

more.title: Cross-border shopping dilutes public revenue less than previously thought
more.summary: Will higher sin taxes, and therefore higher prices, on candy, soft drinks and beer lead to more cross-border shopping? The answer is often assumed to be yes in the public debate, where one of the main arguments against sin taxes on unhealthy products has long been that higher prices will encourage more Danes to shop across the border.
